**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small snack of whole cherry or grape tomatoes (red, oval, about 2–2.5 cm long) on a white paper plate or small bowl. No other food is visible.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A small white plate or bowl, about 15 cm across (judged from the tomato size). Area = 3.14 × (7.5)² ≈ 177 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** About 11 whole cherry tomatoes. No dressing, oil, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The tomatoes cover roughly 20% of the plate area (about 35 cm²). The plate is mostly empty.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about one tomato high (~2 cm). Gross volume ≈ 35 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 70 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** The bulk-density rule gives 70 ml × 0.6 ≈ 42 g. This undercounts, because whole tomatoes are solid fruit and not loose pieces. Counting them individually (each about 2.5 × 2 × 2 cm, roughly 10 g) gives about 11 × 10 g ≈ 110 g. I use the per-fruit estimate.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cherry tomatoes are about 18 kcal per 100 g. 110 g × 18 / 100 ≈ 20 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Eleven cherry tomatoes at about 110 g and 20 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The estimate is an approximation from the photo, not a measurement.

Total: about 110 g, about 20 kcal.
